observations.expected: Two large upper abdominal gas lucencies represent a larger stomach on the patient left and proximal duodenum on the right.
observations.observed: Two large rounded gas lucencies are clearly visible in the upper abdomen. The larger oval lucency with rugal fold impressions is on the patient's left (stomach) and the smaller rounded lucency is on the patient's right (proximal duodenum). Laterality is correct.

observations.expected: Little or no gas is visible distal to the two bubbles within this cropped field.
observations.observed: Below the two upper abdominal gas collections, the abdomen shows uniform soft-tissue/fluid opacity with a complete paucity of bowel gas, consistent with no gas passing beyond the obstruction.

observations.expected: Visible skeletal proportions are compatible with a newborn.
observations.observed: The ribs are thin and gracile, vertebral bodies show immature ossification with cartilaginous end plates, and overall skeletal size and proportions are consistent with a neonate or young infant. No adult-type degenerative changes or advanced ossification centres are present.

findings: Anteroposterior supine abdominal radiograph of a small subject consistent with a neonate or young infant based on osseous size and proportions

Two discrete, large, rounded lucent gas collections are visible in the upper abdomen: one in the right upper quadrant and one in the left upper quadrant, separated by a soft-tissue density midline structure consistent with the spine and surrounding soft tissue

The right-sided gas collection is round and appears to represent a distended gastric antrum or pyloric region; the left-sided gas collection is larger and oval with internal rugal fold impressions, consistent with a distended stomach body/fundus
Together these two gas collections form a 'double bubble' or markedly dilated two-chamber gas pattern in the upper abdomen
The remainder of the abdomen below these two collections shows a uniform soft-tissue/fluid opacity with a paucity of gas, suggesting absence of gas beyond the duodenum
Lower ribs are visible superiorly; the spine demonstrates age-appropriate ossification; the pelvis is not included in the field of view
No pneumoperitoneum is identified; no calcifications are seen
differential: Duodenal atresia or stenosis: the classic 'double bubble' sign representing a dilated stomach and dilated proximal duodenum with no distal bowel gas strongly supports this diagnosis
Duodenal web or intrinsic duodenal obstruction: may produce an identical radiographic appearance and is indistinguishable from atresia on plain film alone
Annular pancreas: extrinsic duodenal obstruction producing a double-bubble pattern; radiographically indistinguishable from intrinsic obstruction without further imaging
anatomyConcerns: Paucity of gas in the lower abdomen is a pathological finding consistent with a complete or near-complete proximal intestinal obstruction rather than a normal variant
The abdomen appears distended and rounded, which is consistent with obstruction in the neonatal period
The pelvis and lower extremities are excluded from the field of view, limiting complete assessment; lateral view or upper GI contrast study would be complementary

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The classic double bubble sign — two large discrete gas-filled lucencies in the upper abdomen with no gas visible distally — is the discriminating finding. The left-sided bubble is larger (stomach) and the right-sided bubble smaller (proximal duodenum), matching the expected laterality for duodenal atresia. While duodenal stenosis, web, and annular pancreas produce an identical plain film appearance, duodenal atresia is the most common and most likely diagnosis in a neonate with a complete double bubble and no distal gas. The independent read's anatomy concerns (distended abdomen, paucity of distal gas) are all explained by the proximal obstruction itself. No unexplained anatomical lesions are identified.
